subject: How to fix error variance to zero ?

messages.author: 177d6b42224d530a
messages.subject: How to fix error variance to zero ?
parts:
Hello,

I am simulating a bifactor model. I would like to fix my error variances to zero. When I changed my values to zero I got the following error message.

Error: lavaan->lav_samplestats_icov():  
   sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

Can someone help in how to set error variances to zero without any issues ?

Thanks

Hereunder is my syntax before setting error variances to zero.


library(simsem)

genmod <- "

  G =~ .7*y1 + .7*y2 + .7*y3 + .7*y4 + .7*y5 + .7*y6 + .7*y7 + .7*y8 + .7*y9
  S1 =~ .2*y1 + .5*y2 + .5*y3
  S2 =~ .5*y4 + .5*y5 + .5*y6
  S3 =~ .5*y7 + .5*y8 + .5*y9
 
  y1 ~~ .47*y1
  y2 ~~ .26*y2
  y3 ~~ .26*y3
  y4 ~~ .26*y4
  y5 ~~ .26*y5
  y6 ~~ .26*y6
  y7 ~~ .26*y7
  y8 ~~ .26*y8
  y9 ~~ .26*y9

  G ~~ 1*G
  S1 ~~ 1*S1
  S2 ~~ 1*S2
  S3 ~~ 1*S3
 
  S1 + S2 + S3 ~~ 0*G
  S1 + S2 ~~ 0*S3
  S1 ~~ 0*S2

"

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: How to fix error variance to zero ?
parts:
Hi, Pierre.

From what I understood, you are writing a population model for a simulation study.
To set the residual variance, change the lines 6-14 to zero. E.g., 'y1 ~~ 0*y1'.

However, note that, by doing so, you'll change the scale of the items, and loadings will be unstandardized (based on a covariance matrix).
Furthermore, only the population residual variance will be zero. The generated samples will oscillate around this value, so I would expect nearly half of the samples to generate observed nonpositive-definite matrices.

Best,
Yago

messages.subject: Re: How to fix error variance to zero ?
parts:
Hi Yago,

Thank you very much for your helpful reply.

This is what I was thinking.

Given this problem I thought before your reply that the best way to simulate zero error variance is to work on matrix.

As a consequence, I started to work with a matrix style on simsem. I have a problem, however, to build my syntax in a matrix style.

I would like to write the syntax for a bifactor model with all factors orthogonal. Unfortunately, I have the following error:

Error in `diag<-`(`*tmp*`, value = paramSet$VTE@free) :
  replacement diagonal has wrong length

Can someone, help me with with syntax ?

Many thanks in advance

Best

library(simsem)

loading <- matrix(0, 9, 4)
loading[1:9, 1] <- NA
loading[1:3, 2] <- NA
loading[4:6, 3] <- NA
loading[7:9, 4] <- NA

loadingValues <- matrix(0, 9, 4)
loadingValues[1:9, 1] <- 0.7  
loadingValues[1:3, 2] <- 0.5
loadingValues[4:6, 3] <- 0.5
loadingValues[7:9, 4] <- 0.5

LY <- bind(loading, loadingValues)
summary(LY)

error.var <- matrix(0, 9, 9)
diag(error.var) <- 1
VTE <- binds(error.var)

error.cor <- matrix(0, 9, 9)
diag(error.cor) <- 1
RTE <- binds(error.cor)

latent.cor <- matrix(NA, 4, 4)
diag(latent.cor) <- 1
RPS <- binds(latent.cor, 0)


CFA.Model <- model(LY = LY, RPS = RPS, RTE = RTE, VTE = VTE, modelType="CFA")

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: How to fix error variance to zero ?
parts:
Hi, Pierre,

I'm afraid I have no experience at using `simsem` in matrix style, but as I see, this will not solve your problem because the zero variance is at the population level, not the sample.
You will either have to simulate several samples to check if the mean residual variance is zero or, in the test model, you will have to restrict the residual variance to zero manually. Note that bifactor models require that all the latent variables are orthogonal to each other, but residual variances do not need to be zero. The only model that requires zero residual variance, as far as I know, is the ACE model for heritability.

Best,
Yago
